lines.trans: You're Toru Muranishi, right?
Cut out the nonsense. Where's the money?
Chairman, you look well. It's in the usual locker.
We're managing to keep the company running somehow, though we've lost customers.
Sorry to put you through such trouble.
Are you still okay to come in three days?
With the chairman absent for so long, all the branch managers are rattled.
Even just showing your face would help.
Understood. I'll go to Hokkaido.
Is Hokkaido cool right now? I've forgotten what kind of clothes to wear.

words.gram: Past た-form of する (to do/happen).

lines.trans: I might be away for a few days.

words.gloss: be known (in かもしれない)

lines.trans: She told you to come back anytime.

words.gram: て-form of 帰る (go/come home), used here as a gentle request.
て-form of auxiliary くる (go do something and return), used as a soft request.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

examples.text: 会長、お元気そうで。いつものロッカーに。
examples.trans: Chairman, you look well. It's in the usual locker.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Everyday word for a business company or one's workplace.

examples.text: 新しい会社に入りました。

examples.trans: The company is near the station.

meanings.en: side or option in comparisons and advice (〜ほうがいい)
meanings.note: Paired with がいい after past or negative forms to recommend the better course ('it is better to...').

examples.text: 早く寝たほうがいいよ。
examples.trans: You had better go to sleep early.

examples.text: 傘を持ったほうがいいです。
examples.trans: It is better to bring an umbrella.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.

examples.trans: Are you still okay to come in three days?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Core everyday reassurance or check covering safety, health, and reliability.

examples.text: 心配しないで、大丈夫だよ。
examples.trans: Do not worry, it is fine.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

examples.text: 長い間会長不在で、支店長がみんな動揺してて。

examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

meanings.note: 分かってる asks or states ongoing understanding; plain past 分かった means 'got it! / I understand'.

examples.text: 日本語が少し分かります。

examples.trans: Got it, I will come right away.

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

examples.text: 北海道、涼しいのか？どんな格好したらいいのか忘れたよ。
examples.trans: Is Hokkaido cool right now? I've forgotten what kind of clothes to wear.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: what kind of; what sort of
meanings.note: Interrogative prenominal modifier.

examples.text: どんな音楽を聴きますか。
examples.trans: What kind of music do you listen to?

examples.text: どんな仕事をしているんですか。
examples.trans: What kind of work do you do?

meanings.note: Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).
Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: Noun.

examples.text: 今日は空がとても青いですね。
examples.trans: The sky is very blue today, isn't it?
Birds are flying in the sky.

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

meanings.note: Short for かもしれない; expresses possibility or uncertainty.
Ichidan verb; most commonly appears in the set expression かもしれない ('might be').

examples.text: 遅れるかもしれません。
本当かもしれませんよ。
examples.trans: It might be true, you know.

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Interrogative pronoun for time.

examples.text: いつまでも待っています。

meanings.en: go home; leave and go back
meanings.note: Repeated past form 帰った、帰った! is an idiomatic shooing command ('off you go, go on home!').

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
